Taylor mode higher order automatic differentiation

Source: R/experimental_jet.R
experimental_jet_jet.Rd

Port of jax.experimental.jet.jet. Where jvp() pushes one tangent through a function, experimental_jet_jet() pushes a truncated Taylor polynomial: given the value h0 of an inner function and its derivatives h1, ..., hK along a direction, it returns the value of fun(h) and its derivatives of order 1 to K, without nesting first order differentiation K times.

Usage

experimental_jet_jet(fun, primals, series, factorial_scaled = TRUE)

Arguments

fun

Function of one or more arrays, returning an array or a pytree of arrays.

primals

List of the arguments of fun: the point of expansion.

series

List with one entry per argument; each entry is the list of the higher order terms of that argument. All entries have the same length, the order of the expansion.

factorial_scaled

If TRUE (the default) the terms of the input and of the output are derivatives. If FALSE they are Taylor coefficients, the derivatives divided by the factorial of their order.

Value

list(primals_out, series_out): the value of fun and, with the same structure, the list of the higher order terms of each output.

Details

Rules exist for the primitives that JAX has rules for (arithmetic, the elementary functions, linear structural operations, reductions, dot_general, convolutions, gathers and scatter-add). As in JAX, control flow primitives have no rule, and custom derivative rules are ignored: the function itself is differentiated.

A rule for another primitive is a function function(primals_in, series_in, params) assigned to the jet field of the primitive object (the counterpart of jet.jet_rules[prim] = rule); it returns list(primal_out, series_out).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# f(h(z)) = sin(z^3) at z = 0.5: h and its first two derivatives go in.
h <- list(0.5^3, 3 * 0.5^2, 6 * 0.5)
out <- experimental_jet_jet(jnp_sin, list(h[[1]]), list(h[2:3]))
out[[1]]        # sin(h0)
out[[2]][[1]]   # cos(h0) * h1
out[[2]][[2]]   # -sin(h0) * h1^2 + cos(h0) * h2
} # }
